results.title: Parity: with only pre-change history (no rotation snapshots) the next group equals the legacy counter for 0-8 completed Giant B, and drafts and other templates are ignored exactly as before
Starting Giant B writes an additive rotation snapshot (group, slots, presented methods); other templates get none; the snapshot equals what is displayed
A Giant B whose presented intensifiers were performed credits its group: the groups then rotate 0,1,2,0,1,2 exactly as before for an athlete who performs them

A finished Giant B in which the presented intensifier was SKIPPED (straight work only) earns no credit: the same group is offered at the next Giant B, and the finished session still counts as a session
A partially done intensifier earns nothing: Myo-Reps with one effort cannot be saved, and a session that finishes after that attempt does not credit the group
Credit policy "any": if a group presents two intensifier slots and only one is performed, the group is credited (the other method waits for the group to come round again)
Interrupted then resumed: a draft that performed the intensifier is credited ONCE; resuming (even after a reload) shows the same methods, and finishing does not credit again
Interrupted before any intensifier: no credit, no lapse count; resuming keeps the same snapshot
No duplicate credit: duplicated session objects and duplicated records (as from a merged restore) credit a group once
Lapse (decision R4 = 2): a group that two consecutive finished sessions presented but nobody performed is moved back, so rotation can never be blocked and the same method is not offered forever
Busy week and COMPACT hide or suppress the intensifier: the session finishes and counts, but the group is not credited
Other templates never move the Giant B rotation, even when they perform intensifiers (Giant B Upper/Lower, Giant A)
A manual intensifier on a slot OUTSIDE the presented group does not credit any group
Legacy history then new sessions: pre-change completed Giant B keep their legacy meaning (no re-judging), and the new era continues from them
Order and clock independence: the derived group does not depend on array order of sessions; every session is judged on its own snapshot
Derivation is read-only and preserves history: calling it writes nothing; legacy sessions and every earlier record stay byte-identical after new sessions

Backup round trip and validation: a session carrying a rotation snapshot restores identically; malformed snapshots (bad group, slots that do not match the group, unknown method, extra keys, markup) are refused
A Giant B started on an older install (draft without a snapshot) resumes safely: no snapshot is invented, the legacy group is displayed, and finishing keeps the legacy credit
Full Session prescriptions unchanged: Giant B set counts per slot and the base slot table are untouched by rotation
